heroText: Victoria is Seychelles' compact capital on Mahé, often noted as one of the world's smallest capital cities, mixing colonial architecture with Creole markets. First-time visitors should browse fresh spices and fish at Sir Selwyn Selwyn-Clarke Market, photograph the miniature Victoria Clock Tower, and wander the Botanical Gardens' giant tortoises. Seychelles International Airport lies a short drive south, and Victoria makes an easy base before heading to Mahé's beaches.

areas.name: Town Centre
areas.text: Town Centre holds Victoria's market, clock tower and government buildings, walkable in an hour and the natural base for a first visit.

areas.name: Beau Vallon
areas.text: Beau Vallon is Mahé's most popular beach, a short drive north of Victoria with beachfront hotels, restaurants and watersports.

areas.name: Eden Island
areas.text: Eden Island is a man-made marina district south of Victoria, offering modern villas, yacht moorings and waterfront dining.

areas.name: Bel Ombre
areas.text: Bel Ombre is a quiet coastal stretch just north of the capital, mixing small guesthouses with easy access to Beau Vallon's beach.

airports.name: Seychelles International Airport (SEZ)
airports.text: Seychelles International Airport sits about 15 minutes south of Victoria, with taxis and hotel transfers covering the short coastal drive.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Seychelles International Airport (SEZ) and central Victoria before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Base in Town Centre for an easy first stay near the market, clock tower and museums, then move to Beau Vallon for Mahé's best beach or Eden Island for marina views. Bel Ombre suits travelers wanting a quiet, beach-adjacent stay close to the capital.
hotelIntro: Victoria hotel choice depends on priorities: Town Centre suits short stays focused on sightseeing and the market, Beau Vallon suits beach-first travelers, and Eden Island or Bel Ombre suit those wanting quieter, resort-style bases nearby.
rentalCars: A rental car is worth having to explore Mahé's beaches and viewpoints beyond Victoria, since taxis are pricier and buses run on limited schedules.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Stay in Town Centre for a night or two of sightseeing, then move to Beau Vallon or another beach for the rest of a Mahé stay.

travelTips.title: Sunday closures
travelTips.text: Plan market visits and shopping for weekdays or Saturday morning, since much of Victoria closes on Sundays.

travelTips.title: Airport transfers
travelTips.text: Book a hotel transfer from Seychelles International Airport in advance, as the drive is short but taxis can be limited late at night.

travelTips.title: Cash and pace
travelTips.text: Carry Seychelles rupees for markets and small vendors, and expect a slow, relaxed pace typical of island life.

nearbyIdeas.label: Beach
nearbyIdeas.text: Beau Vallon Beach is Mahé's liveliest stretch of sand, a short drive from Victoria with watersports, sunset bars and dive centres.

nearbyIdeas.name: Morne Seychellois National Park
nearbyIdeas.label: Nature
nearbyIdeas.text: Morne Seychellois National Park covers most of Mahé's forested interior, with hiking trails and viewpoints above Victoria.

nearbyIdeas.name: Sainte Anne Marine Park
nearbyIdeas.label: Nature
nearbyIdeas.text: Sainte Anne Marine Park protects a cluster of islands offshore, reachable by boat for snorkelling and glass-bottom-boat trips.

history.text: France claimed the Seychelles islands before the settlement that became Victoria developed on Mahe.
French colonists settled the area that later became Victoria, establishing the first town foundation on Mahe.
The British renamed the settlement Victoria after Queen Victoria; it had previously been known as L'Etablissement.
Seychelles became a separate Crown colony, making Victoria the administrative centre of the islands.
Seychelles became independent, and Victoria continued as the capital of the new republic.

history.label: Today
history.text: Modern Victoria concentrates the port, government offices, markets and cultural institutions of Seychelles.
